security_spec.violation_condition: In FreeBSD RISC-V, when running as a guest OS (VS-mode) under a hypervisor that sets henvcfg.CBZE=0 to deny cbo.zero access, or when running as VU-mode userspace with only one of senvcfg.CBZE/henvcfg.CBZE set: the old (pre-fix) spec's operation() pseudocode had three bugs — (1) S/VS-mode was never checked against menvcfg/henvcfg.CBZE, so VS-mode FreeBSD could execute cbo.zero despite henvcfg.CBZE=0; (2) VU-mode used OR semantics ((henvcfg.CBZE | senvcfg.CBZE) == 0) instead of requiring both bits; (3) M-mode incorrectly trapped when menvcfg.CBZE=0. An implementation following the buggy spec would allow cbo.zero to execute across privilege boundaries where it should trap with IllegalInstruction or VirtualInstruction.
security_spec.vulnerability_pattern: cbo.zero operation() access check missing S/VS-mode guard against menvcfg/henvcfg CBZE; VU-mode OR semantics instead of AND for dual-envcfg check
security_spec.summary: Buggy cbo.zero access-check pseudocode allowed VS-mode FreeBSD guest to bypass hypervisor henvcfg.CBZE denial and VU-mode to execute with only one envcfg bit set, violating the two-key RISC-V CBO gating model
